strengths: Valuable dataset contribution: 424 hours of curated primate-centric video addressing the gap of human-centric foundation model pretraining

Strong empirical results: Consistent state-of-the-art performance across four diverse primate behavior benchmarks (PanAf500, ChimpACT, BaboonLand, ChimpBehave) with substantial improvements over baselines
Practical and scalable data curation pipeline: Well-motivated multi-stage filtering using CLIP embeddings (82.8% recall, 90.3% precision) and zero-shot primate detection (82.7 mAPₐₗₗ)
Lightweight and efficient model: 220K-parameter frozen classifier outperforms much larger specialized models (e.g., 167M-parameter ChimpVLM) while scaling favorably with limited labels
Comprehensive ablations: Tables 2, 3, and 5 systematically validate dataset components, continual pretraining benefits, and architectural choices
Clear methodology and presentation: Well-structured paper with detailed technical specifications enabling reproducibility
Commitment to resource release: Authors pledge to release majority of dataset and models, benefiting the research community
weaknesses: Evaluation scope does not match dataset diversity: Only evaluates on chimpanzees and baboons despite dataset containing macaques (43%), orangutans, lemurs, and marmosets; no cross-species generalization analysis undermines 'general-purpose' claims

Lack of statistical rigor: No confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests despite aggregating across 5 classifiers and 3 views; critical for assessing robustness on small datasets (e.g., 2h ChimpACT)

Unexplained continual pretraining anomalies: Table 3 shows counterintuitive accuracy decreases (ChimpACT: −4.72%, PanAf500 B-Acc: −10.9%) that are not analyzed, suggesting potential distribution mismatch or optimization issues

Architectural choices inadequately justified: No comparison of V-JEPA to alternative SSL methods on PriVi data; design decisions (C class tokens, D'=64 projection) appear ad-hoc with minimal ablation effects
Zero-shot detection quality not analyzed: 82.7 mAPₐₗₗ performance could introduce systematic biases; no analysis of failure modes across poses/settings or detection quality variance by dataset source

Reproducibility limitations: 14% of pretraining data cannot be shared; YouTube playlists manually curated (list not provided); relevance classifier trained on only 2,500 images without inter-annotator agreement; training code availability unstated
Missing initialization ablation: Pretraining initialized from VideoMix2M checkpoint; cannot isolate improvements from data vs. architecture vs. initialization
Limited failure analysis: No per-class performance breakdown, no discussion of difficult behavior classes, no error analysis to guide future improvements
Statistical comparison issues: Table 4 has incomplete baseline results; AlphaChimp marked as 'own reproduction' without explanation, complicating direct comparison
Species distribution imbalance: Dataset heavily skewed toward macaques (43%); 5.5% unidentifiable and 3.5% no-primate suggests annotation quality concerns; impact on model learning not discussed

strengths: Addresses genuine application need in primate behavior research with well-motivated shift from human-centric to domain-specific pretraining

Systematic and well-documented data curation pipeline combining multiple filtering techniques (CLIP-based relevance classification, zero-shot primate detection, metadata-based subsampling) with transparent statistics

Comprehensive experimental validation with consistent improvements across four datasets, thorough ablations demonstrating each component's contribution, and appropriate metrics for different evaluation protocols
Practical framework design with parameter-efficient classifier (220k parameters) that scales well to small datasets, balancing frozen evaluation and finetuning
Commitment to reproducibility through promised code/dataset release and sufficient implementation details
weaknesses: Limited algorithmic novelty: uses existing V-JEPA, CLIP embeddings, and Grounding DINO without modification; data curation pipeline closely follows prior work (following approach from cited work [60]); at core, this is application of existing methods to a new domain

Severely overstated 'general-purpose' claims: dataset contains diverse primates but evaluation covers only 2 species (chimpanzees, baboons) despite lemurs, marmosets, orangutans comprising 17.3% of data; requires ground-truth bounding boxes; best results depend on unlabeled in-domain continual pretraining, undermining generalization claims

Confounded results from in-domain continual pretraining: best results (PriVi+CID) combine PriVi pretraining with target-domain pretraining; Table 3 shows +2.68% mAP gains from continual pretraining alone; difficult to isolate PriVi's contribution; requires unlabeled target-domain data, limiting practical applicability

Incremental improvements without statistical significance: 0.96% on BaboonLand, 1.40% on ChimpBehave; no confidence intervals, significance tests, or error bars; training procedure averages five classifiers on three views, suggesting variance is absorbed rather than reported

Incomplete dataset and reproducibility: 14% of pretraining data (camera trap footage) cannot be released due to ongoing research; prevents full verification and reproducibility; undermines claims of reusable community resource

Questionable dataset composition: Table 2 shows YT-Filtered (250h) outperforms R&O (174h) on ChimpACT (37.88 vs 33.01 mAP); no principled justification for including underperforming 174h; missing ablations on size vs. diversity trade-offs; unexplored species imbalance between sources

Incomplete baseline comparisons: AlphaChimp reproduced with incompatible protocols; VideoMAEv2 and InternVideo-L missing results on most datasets; VideoPrism comparisons sparse; different initialization (VideoMix2M) may provide unfair advantage; no comparison to training from scratch with equivalent compute

Evaluation methodology concerns: inconsistent protocols ('best validation accuracy' vs 'end of training'); no hold-out test sets mentioned for some datasets; five-fold CV for ChimpBehave but reporting unclear; risks of overfitting not addressed
Architecture design choices lack justification: downprojection to D'=64 unexplained; C learned class tokens design choice (Table 5 shows effect but not rationale); limited ablation depth

Missing critical analysis: no cross-species generalization studies; no scaling analysis with varying amounts of unlabeled data; no visualization of learned representations; no manual inspection of filtered data quality; no failure case analysis; computational cost of dataset creation not quantified

strengths: Substantial and well-curated dataset contribution (424 hours) addressing a genuine gap in primate-centric pretraining, with commitment to release majority of data and code
Thoughtful, scalable data curation pipeline using CLIP embeddings and zero-shot detection, validated through clear ablations showing each component's contribution
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across four diverse benchmarks with multiple metrics, demonstrating consistent state-of-the-art results across all datasets
Well-designed lightweight frozen classifier (220k params) that outperforms models with 225× more parameters, with clear ablations justifying each architectural choice
Strong empirical results showing improvements over human-centric baselines and fully finetuned models, with favorable scaling to few-label regimes and additional gains from in-domain pretraining
weaknesses: Limited methodological novelty—relies entirely on existing components (V-JEPA, CLIP, Grounding DINO) with contributions primarily in data engineering rather than methods

Overstated generalization claims: evaluation limited to primates (4 datasets, 2-125 minutes each); requires ground truth bounding boxes; no evidence of transfer to other species or significant domain shifts

Data reproducibility concerns: 14% of pretraining data unavailable due to ongoing projects; R&O sourced from institutional collaborations; YouTube data from manually selected playlists limits exact replication

Incomplete data quality analysis: relevance classifier trained on only 2,500 examples; zero-shot detection's false negatives not analyzed; 6% 'No primate' and 9.4% 'Not identifiable' samples retained without justification; no inter-dataset contribution analysis

Unexplained in-domain pretraining results: Table 3 shows contradictory patterns (-9% B-Acc on ChimpACT vs +7.34% on PanAf500), with limited investigation into why broad pretraining outperforms in-domain despite target-domain data availability

Incomplete baseline comparisons: some evaluated on different protocols (AlphaChimp); several baselines report only subset of datasets; missing confidence intervals and statistical significance tests despite multi-run averaging
Limited error analysis: no qualitative failure case study, per-class performance breakdown, or comparison of error patterns versus baselines
Under-justified architectural choices: rationale for multiple CLS tokens vs. alternatives, aggressive 1024→64 downprojection, and 3 attention layers not thoroughly explored
